name: HubSpot
one_liner: HubSpot is a CRM-centered customer platform combining marketing, sales, service, content and data hubs with built-in AI agents and a broad public developer API.

auth.note: Apps must use HubSpot OAuth or a static auth token for single-account apps

access.note: Developer docs get-started flow: install CLI, authorize account, start building; no sales gate shown
API availability varies by subscription tier including Free

api_surface.note: Many APIs across products and tiers

mcp.note: Official remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com
Two official MCP servers: remote CRM and local developer

verdict.note: Documented OAuth/static token auth, rate limits, private and public distribution

notes: Webhooks are supported (webhook subscriptions per app), alongside REST. Legacy private app tokens/static auth tokens are single-account. The pages do not show the exact signup flow for free accounts, but the tier page lists a Free tier. Public marketplace distribution of apps has separate rate limits and certification. Remote MCP requires a user-level app with OAuth; OAuth 2.1/PKCE migration is planned. The specific API-key mechanism is described as a static auth token or legacy private app token.

name: fanbasis
one_liner: FanBasis, now apparently rebranded as Commas, is a creator-commerce platform combining checkout, payments, webinars, courses and communities for online sellers.

auth.note: API docs are behind a password login; no auth method is publicly documented.

access.note: Developer docs require a password, so access is gated.
APIs and SDKs are listed under an 'Enterprise & APIs' offering, and the FAQ mentions a FanBasis-to-Commas rename.

api_surface.note: Marketing page mentions APIs and SDKs for embedded checkouts and payouts; no public reference.

mcp.note: Vendor's site lists an MCP integration marked beta.

verdict.note: Password-gated docs block building without vendor approval.
An API and an MCP beta exist, but no public docs.

notes: FanBasis appears to have rebranded to Commas (the FAQ has 'What happened to FanBasis?'; the answer was not shown). The API docs at dev-docs.fanbasis.com are password-protected, and how to get the password is not shown. Auth methods and API type are not documented in the fetched pages. 'custom_other' stands for undocumented auth, and 'rest' is an inference from the marketing mention of APIs. The access class 'gated_sales' is an inference from the 'Enterprise & APIs' positioning. The MCP is described as beta on the vendor site, but no server URL or docs were found, so mcp_url points to the homepage. Unrelated pages in the fetched set (Fabric, Supabase, Webflow, commareports.com) are about other products and were ignored.
